editorial.headline: Government Workforce Training Is Public Work, Not a PMA Entry Point
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers government-run workforce training built around industry and user needs, but it is closed to foreign investment nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
Government Workforce Training covers work training managed by the government to raise competence through programmes shaped around the needs of industry and users. It is meant to translate those identified needs into practical skills development. Its examples span information and communications technology, creative industries, tourism and hospitality, business and management, domestic workers, agriculture and fisheries, and other government workforce-training programmes. The defining feature is governance: this is a government-managed training function, not a general private training activity.

The record identifies no business scale as open to this activity. More importantly, it marks the national PMA status as TERTUTUP, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 0%. For a foreign-owned applicant, that is the complete national position: this activity is not available for PMA registration. The listed policy source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Training may respond directly to industry or user demand, but that does not alter the stated character of the activity as government-managed workforce development.

In Bali, the position also remains closed: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. The explanation, however, deserves precision. The record identifies it as medium-high/high risk, requires verification by address, and states that it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. That moratorium blocks PMA across Bali for Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. It is therefore not the stated reason for this activity’s closed Bali status.

The distinction matters because it prevents a misleading shortcut. The medium-high/high risk label is not permission: this government-managed activity is closed to PMA nationally and in Bali. Its scope may be broad in subject matter, but the organising premise does not change. The record supplies no open business scale and no PMA registration route, whether considered nationally or in Bali.
